LESSON: LANGUAGE USE 9.3.1 OPPOSITES

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade three
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.3: Language Use 9.3.1 Opposites
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Language Use 9.3.1 Opposites, part of Strand 9 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade three General.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to learn about opposites of words?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. recognise signs of vocabulary related to the theme for effective communication,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Language Use 9.3.1 Opposites in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. identify the opposites of different words for effective communication,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Language Use 9.3.1 Opposites in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. use opposites to construct sentences related to the theme,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Language Use 9.3.1 Opposites in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. value the role of opposites in communicating ideas. • In pairs, learners are guided to watch a demonstration or signed video clip with vocabulary on the theme wild animals. • Individually, learner is guided to identify, fingerspell and sign vocabulary related to the theme wild animals. • Individually, learner is guided to identify and sign opposites from a group of words in a text. • In groups, learners are guided to tell stories as they sign about wildlife conservation using the opposites of a variety of words, with peers. • In pairs, learners are guided to construct signed sentences using the opposites of words related to the theme, with peers. • In pairs, learners are guided to use opposites to respond to questions from a story, poem or a conversation. • In groups, learners are guided to play a language game that involves identifying and signing opposites of different words. Why is it important to learn about opposites of words? 89

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Language Use 9.3.1 Opposites in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. value the role of opposites in communicating ideas. • In pairs, learners are guided to watch a demonstration or signed video clip with vocabulary on the theme wild animals. • Individually, learner is guided to identify, fingerspell and sign vocabulary related to the theme wild animals. • Individually, learner is guided to identify and sign opposites from a group of words in a text. • In groups, learners are guided to tell stories as they sign about wildlife conservation using the opposites of a variety of words, with peers. • In pairs, learners are guided to construct signed sentences using the opposites of words related to the theme, with peers. • In pairs, learners are guided to use opposites to respond to questions from a story, poem or a conversation. • In groups, learners are guided to play a language game that involves identifying and signing opposites of different words. Why is it important to learn about opposites of words? 89

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Language Use 9.3.1 Opposites together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Creativity and Imagination: as the learner tells stories about wildlife conservation using the opposites of a variety of words.

● Self-efficacy: as learner uses opposites correctly to respond to questions from a story, poem or a conversation.

Values:
Love: sharing as the learner shares stories about wildlife with peers.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills: Effective communication is developed as the learner uses opposites of words in speech correctly.

Links to other Learning Areas:
The learner applies the knowledge on opposites to learning of similar concept in Kenya Sign Language.

Suggested Learning Resources

Assistive devices fitted with appropriate technology such as Hearing aids and amplifiers, signed audio-visual recordings, print or digital stories, pocket

charts, print and digital flash cards

Main points to remember:

1. recognise signs of vocabulary related to the theme for effective communication,
2. identify the opposites of different words for effective communication,
3. use opposites to construct sentences related to the theme,
